def: Constructing the input columns a model receives from raw data so that the useful pattern is easy for the model to find.
Representing a categorical column as one 0/1 column per category, so a linear model can give each category its own offset.
Replacing each category by how often it occurs in the training data, giving one column whatever the cardinality.
The number of distinct values a categorical column takes.
Replacing each category by a summary of the target within it, usually the mean, which is powerful for high-cardinality columns and leaks the label unless done out of fold.
Blending a category's mean with the overall mean, weighted by the category's row count, so small categories are not trusted too much.
Encoding each training row with statistics computed only from the other folds, so no row's feature contains its own label.
Target encoding that removes each row's own label from its category mean, which leaves a reversed copy of the label within each category.
A summary of an entity's event history, such as a count, sum or recency, computed over a window.
The moment a prediction is made; every feature must be computed from information dated before it.
Recency, frequency and monetary value: three classic customer aggregates built from purchase history.
A column combining two or more inputs, such as a product, ratio or difference, so a model can use a relationship it could not see from either alone.
Representing a wrap-around quantity such as the hour of day by its sine and cosine so that the ends of the cycle sit next to each other.
Judging a feature or group of features by retraining without it under the same validation and comparing the scores.
